question: What can the DJI Matrice 30T be set to do when the remote controller signal is lost?

intake.decided_by: code (single pass has no intake call)

brief.short_answer: Claims indicate the M30T can trigger RTH, hover, or landing when RC link is lost, per manual; FAA guidance urges attempting to reestablish the link and to initiate loss-of-control procedures if it fails. Incident reports corroborate loss-of-link events with RTH activation and external interference issues, though unverifiable in some cases. Overall, the aircraft supports configurable failsafe actions upon signal loss, with RTH as a common automatic response. There are gaps in confirming cause of interference and consistency across incidents.

sections.label: FAA guidance
sections.abstain_reason: no claims in the single-pass brief

claims.text: When the remote controller signal is lost, the action of the aircraft can be set to RTH, land, or hover in DJI Pilot 2.
claims.quote: The action of the aircraft when the remote controller signal is lost can be set to RTH, land, or hover in Camera View > > > Signal Lost Action in DJI

claims.text: If RTH is selected and the RC link is lost, the aircraft will start RTH using Advanced RTH and will remain in RTH even if the RC signal is restored.
claims.quote: The aircraft will start RTH using Advanced RTH according to the RTH settings. The aircraft will remain in RTH even if the remote controller signal is restored.

claims.text: If the remote controller signal is lost and the RTH is canceled, the Intelligent Battery may not have enough power for the aircraft to land safely, which may lead to the aircraft crashing or being lost.
claims.quote: If RTH is canceled following the warning, the Intelligent Battery may not have enough power for the aircraft to land safely, which may lead to the aircraft crashing or being lost.

gaps.text: Verification of the exact RTH mode or failsafe sequence changes when RC signal returns is not consistently described across sections.
Unverified reports in incident: interference near antenna and its causal link to lost link are not independently confirmed.
